## Answer

$$\int_0^1x^2\ln^n x\,dx=\frac{(-1)^n n!}{3^{n+1}}.$$

Set $t=-\ln x$. Then the integral becomes

$$(-1)^n\int_0^\infty t^ne^{-3t}\,dt,$$

which is $(-1)^n\Gamma(n+1)/3^{n+1}$.

## Answer

Writing $\tan^n x=\tan^{n-2}x(\sec^2x-1)$ gives

$$I_n+I_{n-2}=\frac1{n-1}\quad(n\ge2).$$

With $I_0=\pi/4$ and $I_1=\tfrac12\ln2$, this yields

$$I_{2m}=(-1)^m\frac\pi4+\sum_{j=1}^m\frac{(-1)^{m-j}}{2j-1},$$

$$I_{2m+1}=(-1)^m\frac{\ln2}{2}+\sum_{j=1}^m\frac{(-1)^{m-j}}{2j}.$$

Since $0<\tan x<1$ inside $(0,\pi/4)$, $I_{n+2}<I_n<I_{n-2}$. Combining this with $I_{n+2}+I_n=1/(n+1)$ and $I_n+I_{n-2}=1/(n-1)$ gives

$$\frac1{2(n+1)}<I_n<\frac1{2(n-1)}.$$

## Answer

Using $\sin A-\sin B=2\cos[(A+B)/2]\sin[(A-B)/2]$,

$$I_n-I_{n-1}=2\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos((2n-1)x)\,dx=(-1)^{n-1}\frac2{2n-1}.$$

Also $I_1=2$. Hence

$$I_3=2-\frac23+\frac25=\boxed{\frac{26}{15}},$$

which is the requested value of $\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin6x/\sin x\,dx$.

## Answer

$$\int_0^1\frac{\arctan\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x}(1+x)}\,dx=\frac{\pi^2}{16}.$$

Set $t=\arctan\sqrt{x}$. Then the integrand times $dx$ becomes $2t\,dt$, and the limits are $0$ and $\pi/4$.

## Answer

$$\int_0^3\arcsin\sqrt{\frac{x}{1+x}}\,dx=\frac{4\pi}{3}-\sqrt3.$$

For $x\ge0$, $\arcsin\sqrt{x/(1+x)}=\arctan\sqrt{x}$. Put $t=\sqrt{x}$ and integrate $2t\arctan t$ by parts from $0$ to $\sqrt3$.

## Answer

$$\int_0^1\arctan\sqrt{\frac{x}{1-x}}\,dx=\frac\pi4.$$

Set $x=\sin^2\theta$. The inverse tangent becomes $\theta$, and the integral is

$$\int_0^{\pi/2}\theta\sin2\theta\,d\theta=\frac\pi4.$$

## Answer

$$\int_{e^{1/4}}^{e^{1/2}}\frac{dx}{x\sqrt{\ln x(1-\ln x)}}=\frac\pi6.$$

First set $t=\ln x$, then $t=\sin^2\theta$. The transformed integral is $2\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/4}d\theta=\pi/6$.

## Answer

$$I=\frac1e-1.$$

Let $u=\sqrt{x}$. Then

$$I=2\int_0^1\left(\int_1^ue^{-t^2}\,dt\right)du=-2\int_0^1\left(\int_u^1e^{-t^2}\,dt\right)du.$$

Reversing the order over $0\le u\le t\le1$ gives $-2\int_0^1te^{-t^2}\,dt=e^{-1}-1$.

## Proof

Let $F(u)=\int_0^uf(t)\,dt$. Integration by parts gives

$$\int_0^1F(\sqrt{x})\,dx=F(1)-\int_0^1x^2f(x)\,dx,$$

and

$$\int_0^1F(x^2)\,dx=F(1)-\int_0^1\sqrt{x}f(x)\,dx.$$

Subtracting these identities proves

$$\int_0^1\left[\int_{x^2}^{\sqrt{x}}f(t)\,dt\right]dx=\int_0^1(\sqrt{x}-x^2)f(x)\,dx.$$

## Proof

The region $0\le x\le1$, $x\le t\le\sqrt{x}$ is equivalently

$$0\le t\le1,\qquad t^2\le x\le t.$$

Therefore reversing the integration order gives

$$\int_0^1\int_x^{\sqrt{x}}\frac{\sin t}{t}\,dt\,dx=\int_0^1\frac{\sin t}{t}(t-t^2)\,dt=\int_0^1(1-t)\sin t\,dt=1-\sin1.$$

## Answer

$$\int_{-1}^1x\ln(1+e^x)\,dx=\frac13.$$

Pair the values at $x$ and $-x$. Since

$$\ln(1+e^x)-\ln(1+e^{-x})=x,$$

the symmetric integral becomes $\int_0^1x\cdot x\,dx=1/3$.

## Answer

$$\int_0^{\pi a}y^3\,dx=\frac{35\pi a^4}{8}.$$

Here $dx=a(1-\cos t)dt$ and $y=a(1-\cos t)$, so the integral is

$$a^4\int_0^\pi(1-\cos t)^4dt=32a^4\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^8u\,du=\frac{35\pi a^4}{8}.$$

## Answer

$$\int_0^2|x-x^2|\,dx=1.$$

The expression changes sign at $x=1$, so

$$\int_0^1(x-x^2)dx+\int_1^2(x^2-x)dx=\frac16+\frac56=1.$$

## Answer

$$I=\ln2\,\ln3.$$

Set $u=e^x$ in each integral. Then shift $u=v+1$ in the second one to obtain

$$I=\int_1^2\left[\frac{\ln u}{u+1}+\frac{\ln(u+1)}u\right]du.$$

The bracket is the derivative of $\ln u\ln(u+1)$, so evaluation at $1$ and $2$ gives $\ln2\ln3$.
